user.title: Vidaa TV
user.description: Enter the IP address of your Vidaa TV.

certs.title: SSL Certificates
certs.description:
Most TVs require client certificates for mTLS authentication. Place the certificate files in `{cert_dir}/` or specify custom paths below.

Required files: `{cert_file}` and `{key_file}`

Older TVs expose a plain, unencrypted MQTT broker and reject TLS - for those, turn off "Use SSL/TLS" and no certificates are needed.

data_description.use_ssl: Leave on for the usual encrypted connection. Turn off only if setup fails to connect and your TV runs older firmware that speaks plain MQTT - then the certificate paths below are ignored and the static login is used automatically.
data_description.auth_mode: How credentials are generated. "Auto" detects your TV's protocol version and falls back if the TV rejects it. Choose "Static" if your TV runs older firmware and setup fails with a not-authorized error; "Dynamic" forces the newer scheme.

init.title: VIDAA Eco options
init.description:
Settings for this TV. Everything here is optional unless you use **Auto power-off**.

**MAC addresses reported by this TV**  
{known_macs}

**Network throughput (needed for Auto power-off)**  
A TV does not report whether an open app is actually playing, so Auto power-off reads the TV's network traffic from your router integration (for example UniFi "bandwidth sensors" or FRITZ!Box). Sensors found automatically for this TV's MAC address:  
{detected}

Not using Auto power-off? Ignore this section - the remote, buttons and media player work without it. Step-by-step guide: [Network throughput]({docs_url})

data_description.scan_interval: How often to poll the TV for state updates (in seconds).
data_description.wol_mac: MAC address to send the Wake-on-LAN packet to when turning the TV on. Leave empty to use the default. A magic packet only reaches the interface the TV is actually connected on, so if turning the TV on does not work, try the other address listed above. The TV must also have Wake-on-LAN enabled in its network settings.
data_description.auth_mode: How credentials are generated. "Auto" detects your TV's protocol version and falls back if the TV rejects it. Choose "Static" if your TV runs older firmware and setup fails with a not-authorized error; "Dynamic" forces the newer scheme.
data_description.throughput_floor_kbps: Below this total traffic (kbit/s) an open app counts as 'nothing playing' and the idle timer can start. 100 kbit/s suits most streaming apps; raise it if a paused app keeps trickling data.
data_description.throughput_auto: Use the data-rate sensors that another integration (UniFi, FRITZ!Box, ...) attaches to a device with this TV's MAC address - the list above. Ignored when you pick sensors below.
data_description.throughput_sensors: Pick one or more sensors that measure this TV's traffic (download, upload or both - they are added together). Pick both the Wi-Fi and the Ethernet client if your TV can use either. Any data-rate unit works (bit/s, kbit/s, Mbit/s, kB/s, MB/s ...). **Required while Auto power-off is on**, unless sensors were found automatically. Leave empty to use automatic detection.

error.throughput_required: Auto power-off is on, but no throughput sensor was found or picked. Pick at least one sensor, or turn off the TV's Auto power-off switch first. See the guide linked above.

confirm.title: Add SSL Certificates
confirm.description:
The Vidaa TV integration requires SSL certificates for authentication.

Please place the following files in `{cert_dir}/`:
- `{cert_file}`
- `{key_file}`

These can be extracted from the Vidaa APK. Click Submit after adding the files.

abort.certificates_still_missing: Certificates are still missing. Please add the required files.

init.title: Reconnect to TV
init.description:
The connection to your Vidaa TV at {host} has failed.

Please ensure:
1. The TV is powered on
2. The TV is connected to the network
3. No firewall is blocking port 36669

Click Submit to acknowledge and retry.

throughput_missing.title: {tv}: Auto power-off has no throughput sensor
throughput_missing.description:
Auto power-off is on for **{tv}**, but no network throughput sensor is configured or could be found. Without one, an open app (Netflix, YouTube...) never counts as idle, so the TV will only power off from the home screen or an input without signal.

Fix it under **Settings > Devices & services > VIDAA Eco > Configure**, or turn Auto power-off off. Step-by-step guide: [Network throughput]({url})
